name: Wari state brewing of chicha at Cerro Baúl
summary: The Wari empire ran an industrial-scale brewery on the Cerro Baúl mesa in southern Peru, able to brew hundreds of gallons of pepper-berry chicha each week.
description: The Wari built a brewery in their city on the Cerro Baúl mesa in southern Peru, with fire pits and large ceramic vats able to produce hundreds of gallons of brew a week. The excavators describe the drink as chicha based on pepper-tree berries and infer from shawl pins on the floor that the brewers were elite women. The Wari held the site from about 600 to about 1000 CE and burned the brewery when they left.

impact.note: State brewing served one society, the Wari (reach 1); it scaled up a drink people already made (depth 1); no later development is shown to rest on it (generativity 0).

date.label: between c. 600 and c. 1000 CE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The Wari settled Cerro Baúl about 600 CE and left about 1000 CE, burning their brewery as they went, so the brewery dates within that span.

evidence.supports: The Wari settled the site around A.D. 600 and then departed abruptly around 1000 for reasons that remain mysterious. The archaeological evidence shows that they torched the brewery, then tossed serving pitchers and ceremonial ceramic drinking vessels into the embers.

date.label: c. 1000 CE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The excavators described the Wari brewery at Cerro Baúl as about 1,000 years old, industrial in scale, and apparently the oldest in the Andes.

evidence.supports: the 1,000-year-old industrial scale brewery, built by the largest empire to predate the Inca, appeared to be the oldest in the Andes mountains

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Coordinates of Cerro Baúl are from the supervisor's memory (about 17.11 S, 70.86 W), not from a fetched source, and must be checked.
The lead's subject, the earliest maize chicha in the Andes, is still open: no source for it was fetched.
Whether the Cerro Baúl brew also used maize, and when within 600 to 1000 CE the brewery was built, need the Moseley et al. 2005 PNAS report, which could not be fetched.
This record is close to a single instance; it should hang from a wider record of Andean brewing once one exists.

research.note: No fetched source says Andean brewing arose independently; the sources only date the Wari brewery.
